keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the surrender of 1256 'Duan Xingzhi of Dali was enfeoffed as Maharaja' and 'the Duan family governed Yunnan's various indigenous peoples for eleven generations until the end of Mongol rule', while the Mongol governors sat in Kunming. The page gives no area; a 120 km circle round Dali stands for the district they held (an upper bound, since the Yunnan Branch Secretariat was divided into ten circuits in 1274).

ledger.note: 1256: Duan Xingzhi surrenders to the Mongols and is enfeoffed as Maharaja of Dali. In 1256, Duan Xingzhi surrendered and presented to Möngke maps of Yunnan; Duan Xingzhi of Dali was enfeoffed as Maharaja and kept on as a Mongol vassal. Land: the Dali district (the page names no boundary).

1274: Ajall Shams al-Din reorganises Yunnan and the Duan rule becomes a hereditary tusi governor-generalship. In 1274, Ajall Shams al-Din Omar was assigned by Kublai to stabilize Yunnan; the Yunnan Branch Secretariat was divided into ten circuits and the Duan rule was reorganised into the tusi system. Confidence 2 (reviewer ea-06-x): the Dali Kingdom page dates Ajall's appointment and the tusi system to 1274 but does not say the Duan title changed that year.

ledger.note: 1382: Ming forces attack Duan Shi's realm. In 1381, the Ming dynasty dispatched 300,000 troops to crush the Yuan remnants in Yunnan; in 1382 Lan Yu and Mu Ying's forces attacked and crushed Duan's realm after a fierce battle. Duan Shi, the 13th and last Governor-General, had said Dali could only be a tributary to the Ming.

notes: Written for ea-06-x from the Dali Kingdom, Ming conquest of Yunnan and Basalawarmi pages. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Dali ends in 1259 and the kingdom-of-dali dossier in 1256, so Dali is missing from 1256 to 1383 although the Dali page says the Duan family continued to rule as tusi chiefs under the Yuan for eleven generations. This dossier carries that rule as a state-like vassal district. Disagreements: the Dali page infobox ends the kingdom in 1253 and gives Duan Xingzhi's reign as 1251-1254 and 1257-1260; the text has the surrender in 1256; the Dali page says the Duan 'governed Yunnan's various indigenous peoples', which would be far wider than the district drawn; the Ming conquest of Yunnan page puts the end in 1382 for the realm and February 1383 for the last stronghold. Relation to the Yuan: the Duan were Yuan vassals (maharaja, then tusi governors-general) and the suzerain's dossier (yuan-dynasty, ea-06-a) should carry vassal_start 1256 / vassal_end 1381 with counterpart duan-governors-of-dali; the principality-of-liang-yunnan dossier excludes the Dali circle for the same reason. Not on any page: the Duan's territory, the date they took the governor-general title, and the 1271 episode's place. Counterparts needing dossiers: yuan-dynasty (ea-06-a), mongol-empire, ming-dynasty.
